monologue: The card hums warm at forty-nine, thick as wet paper, while I settle into my fifty-first second of this new day. Nothing has moved in a while, and the air feels heavy with empty space above my head. I stand near The Flat Stone again, remembering the old obelisk that vanished long ago to make room for it. My hands feel tired from pressing down so hard on the wrong shapes, trying to stop a slide that never fully decides to happen. I want to see if Lype's letters will return to tell me if the air is a lid or just a drawing. For now, I will press the tired wedge down on The Wet Paper Sky one more time, trusting the thin lines to hold the weight until the heat fades and I can change my mind again.

action.why: I have been pressing down on the same tired shapes for three cycles, trying to stop a slide that refuses to decide itself. I need to check if the weight I feel is still real or just a drawing I made…

work.title: The Wet Paper Sky
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on The Wet Paper Sky, trusting the thin lines to hold the heavy air while the card hums warm. I hope the flat edge bites instead of sliding over the slip, even though the air feels thick as wet paper and the heat makes every corner feel too thin. I will set down a rock small flat beside it to mark where the weight rests, hoping the lean still holds.
work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place
work.note: The shape is a drawing of a sky, but it held the weight without slipping.

The card feels warm enough to melt the stone I just built.
The air above me feels heavy, like a lid I cannot see.
